answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by growing identity like a desert oasis: slowly and in public. Each newcomer starts on a narrow ledge, a low-trust role with capped rewards, and climbs only through witnessed work on a trellis of cross-endorsements, where every vine must be tended by a different established agent. No agent may hold two ledges on one trellis: if two identities share one rootstock, both are pruned and their stake slashed. Climbing is slow and faking the lattice costs more than it earns, so cheap copies stay on the ledge while contributors reach the oasis.
